subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust lifecycle for generated HTML after outbound staging?
rationale: The patch fixes a real message-delivery regression, but it deliberately widens a local host-read HTML trust boundary and adds persistent provenance state; automation should not decide that security lifecycle without owner intent.

options.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle After Rebase
options.body: A maintainer/security owner accepts the content-bound SQLite provenance design and the contributor refreshes the conflicting branch before merge.

options.title: Require A Narrower Boundary
options.body: Ask for a revised design that changes marker ownership, cleanup, persistence, or failure behavior before landing.

options.title: Keep Staged HTML Fail-Closed
options.body: Pause or close the PR and keep outbound-staged generated HTML blocked if the expanded trust lifecycle is not worth owning.

recommendation.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle After Rebase
recommendation.body: A maintainer/security owner accepts the content-bound SQLite provenance design and the contributor refreshes the conflicting branch before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam being extended here.
